value.body: Many chartered accountants work inside companies rather than in practice — in financial reporting, accounts and controllership, taxation, internal audit, treasury, budgeting and business finance. A CA in employment does not need ICAI's Certificate of Practice and works as a salaried employee.

items.label: Certificate of Practice
items.note: Needed only to practise, such as signing audit reports

items.label: Typical first role
items.value: Executive or assistant manager in finance

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Qualify as a CA (Foundation, Intermediate, articleship, Final) and become an ICAI member. Companies hire through ICAI's campus placement programmes, direct applications and referrals; audit-firm experience is a common bridge into industry roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Industry roles bring a fixed salary and a defined ladder towards finance head or CFO; practice brings independence, with income tied to building clients.
The sector you start in (manufacturing, banking and financial services, IT and so on) shapes later options.
Ind AS, GST, ERP systems and spreadsheet modelling are widely asked for.
Some CAs move between practice and industry over their careers.
